title: Performance evaluation: positions, competencies and review cycles

text.Nastavení slovního popisu stupnice: Setting the verbal description of the scale
text.Vyberte možnost vytvoření dotazníku: Select the option to create a questionnaire
text.Jak se vám daří plnit cíle za uplynulé o: How well are you meeting your goals for the past period?

s01.narration: Reviews in spreadsheets and notes scattered across emails? Hi, I'm Maria from the Sloneek team, and I'll show you performance evaluation.

s02.narration: Evaluation is built on positions and their competencies. Managers evaluate their direct reports, and people can also evaluate themselves.

s03.narration: In the left menu, I click Performance evaluation. Here you see all review cycles, their status, and their completion rate.

s04.narration: The filters above the table quickly separate drafts, ongoing cycles, cycles ready to launch, and completed ones.

s05.narration: Let's start with positions. The Manage positions button opens an overview of job positions and their competencies.

s06.narration: For each position, you see how many people hold it and how many competencies its competency model contains.

s07.narration: I'll open the Customer Support Specialist position. At the top are the name and the job description, which the employee sees too.

s08.narration: Below is the competency model. Each competency has its own scale, here zero to five, and you can describe each level in words.

s09.narration: You don't have to invent competencies yourself: type the position into the AI field and AI suggests them. You then assign the position to people in their profile.

s10.narration: Now let's create a new cycle. I click Create and fill in a name, for example Performance review for Q4.

s11.narration: The first option adds competencies from the job positions to the questionnaire. The manager always evaluates, and I'll also tick self-evaluation.

s12.narration: Under Targeting, you choose who gets evaluated: the whole company, teams, locations, tags, positions, or specific people. I'll pick selected users.

s13.narration: In the Timeline, I set the start and end date. The cycle can even start today.

s14.narration: I click Next. The review is saved as a draft, and we move on to the questionnaire.

s15.narration: AI can draft the questionnaire for you, or you can start from scratch. I'll choose Start from scratch.

s16.narration: In Instructions, you write separate guidance for the self-evaluation and for the manager. All changes are saved automatically.

s17.narration: In All positions, you add questions for everyone being evaluated. I click Add question and type the wording.

s18.narration: As the answer type, I choose a scale from one to five. A question can be for the manager only, or for both the manager and the user.

s19.narration: Each position has questions from its competency model. You can add your own questions here, too.

s20.narration: I click Next. The summary shows the name, targeting, dates, and the number of questions.

s21.narration: The Launch button starts the cycle, and evaluators get their tasks. For this demo, I'll leave it as a draft.

s22.narration: Now the results. In the overview, I open the demo review for the third quarter.

s23.narration: At the top, you see the number of participants and the completion rate. The Results table shows who's still missing a type of feedback.

s24.narration: In the Raters tab, you check who evaluates whom. In the Results table, I click the name of the person being evaluated.

s25.narration: The report shows strengths and areas to improve: here, customer communication leads and independence is the weakest. AI key observations sum it up in words.

s26.narration: Detailed feedback shows the manager's rating next to the self-evaluation. You set the agreed final result with the pencil icon.

s27.narration: You can turn a weaker area straight into a personal goal. The shared notes hold the agreed action plan, which the employee sees too.

s28.narration: And the employee's view? They open My performance evaluation. While a cycle is running, the questionnaire waits in My tasks.

s29.narration: My cycles holds their results, and the Competencies tab shows the position description and what they'll be evaluated on.

s30.narration: A final tip: duplicate a finished cycle in the overview, and your next review round is ready in no time.

s31.narration: Now you know how to set up positions, prepare a review cycle, and read the results. If something doesn't work, check the Help Center.

s32.narration: Less admin, more time for people. This is Sloneek.
